summary: George Chemparathy was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Paul Hacker (~1961–1964) and Erich Frauwallner (~1965–1969), and held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and Utrecht University as Professor (~1974–1993).

George Cowgill worked in history and archaeology, having studied at Stanford (~1948–1952) and Harvard (~1956–1963). He served on the faculty at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2018).

George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London. He spent his career as a faculty member at University College London from ~1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès worked in archaeology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at EPHE, EFEO, and the University of Berlin. He directed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929) and the EFEO (1929–1947), later teaching at INALCO and the Sorbonne.

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968–1972), where he became Professor of Religion around 1974.

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago (1902) and Harvard (1903–1905). He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George E. Dunkel is a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins (1975–1978) and Princeton (1978–1986) before taking the Indo-European chair at Zurich in 1986.

George Foot Moore was a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale (1870–1872) and Union Theological Seminary (~1874–1877). He was a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and Harvard University (1902; 1904–1928).
George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who studied at Phillips Academy (~1856–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He held an academic post at Harvard University from ~1870 to 1913.

George L. Hart is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard (~1963–1971). He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1974) and served as professor at UC Berkeley (~1974–2014).

George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher. He studied at MIT (~1958–1962) and Indiana University (~1962–1966), taught linguistics at Harvard (1965–1969), and served as professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley (1972–2016).

George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins. He held professorships at the Catholic University of America (1895–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1939), and was LSA president in 1931.

George Quasha is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology. He founded Barrytown/Station Hill Press and taught at Stony Brook University (~1968–1971), Bard College (~1974–2005), The New School, and Naropa University.
George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman (attested 1978).
George Saintsbury was educated at King's College School (~1858–1863) and Merton College (~1863–1868). He held a post at the University of Edinburgh from ~1895 to 1915.
Philosopher George Santayana studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Cambridge, earning his PhD under William James. He served on the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.
George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Cambridge (BA until 1864) and the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).

Indologist George Thibaut studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He was director at Queen's College/Government Sanskrit College in Benares, principal at Muir Central College and Sanskrit College, and registrar at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta.
George Turnour was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and historian who served in the Ceylon Civil Service starting in 1818 and was an honorary member of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1836–1843).

George Uglow Pope was an Indologist and linguist who founded and led Breeks Memorial School and Bishop Cotton Boys' School. He later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford (~1884–1907).
